title: Shrinking refining finite clopen partitions
statement: Let $S$ be a compact metric totally disconnected space in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. There exist finite partitions $P_i$ of $S$ into nonempty sets, indexed by positive natural numbers, with $P_{i+1}$ refining $P_i$ and every atom clopen of diameter strictly less than $(1/2)^i$. Empty $S$ is permitted, with empty partitions.

source.place: Tag 08ZZ, lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering, lines 4206–4229; the shrinking metric common-refinement specialization is the parent theorem docstring step 1.

proof.text: For each positive real radius epsilon, cover S by open balls of radius epsilon/3. Use the clopen-basis refinement [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-clopen-basis], in its Mathlib finite disjoint refinement form TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover.exists_finite_nonempty_disjoint_clopen_cover. Its nonempty disjoint clopen sets form a Finpartition. Each is contained in a ball of radius epsilon/3 and thus has diameter at most 2 epsilon/3, strictly less than epsilon.

Choose such a partition Q_i with epsilon=(1/2)^i. Define P_1=Q_1 and P_(i+1)=P_i inf Q_(i+1). The infimum partition has the nonempty intersections as atoms, so all atoms are clopen. P_(i+1) refines P_i and P_i refines Q_i. Diameter monotonicity gives the required bound. This also works for empty S.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_shrinking_clopen_partitions
    (S : Type u) [MetricSpace S] [CompactSpace S] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace S] :
    ∃ P : ℕ+ → Finpartition (Set.univ : Set S),
      (∀ i, P (i + 1) ≤ P i) ∧
      (∀ i p, p ∈ (P i).parts → IsClopen p ∧ Metric.diam p < (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ))
